verdict.rationale: AWS Budgets is documented for tracking costs and usage, with alerts on both actual and forecasted spend and automated budget actions such as applying an IAM policy that blocks new provisioning. That covers the budgets and alerts parts of the story. No evidence in the pack documents spend anomaly detection, which is an explicit element of the story. Missing for 10: documented cost anomaly detection, explicit evidence that budgets are configurable from account creation (day one), independent or hands-on corroboration of alert behavior.

support.subject: As a founder, the bill cannot silently explode — budgets, alerts, and documented anomaly detection on spend, configurable from day one

citations.quote: You can use AWS Budgets to track and take action on your AWS costs and usage.
You can choose to be alerted for both actual (after accruing) and forecasted (before accruing) spends.
you could automatically apply a custom IAM policy that denies you the ability to provision additional resources within an account.
